description: A home-recording hobbyist must decide whether to host a neighborhood musician's live recording session in a community room in exchange for music lessons, while settling the session details, compensation, a legally unusable competing cash offer, and permitted use of the recording.

agents.name: Elena
agents.role: Recording Setup Owner and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: Elena has a portable multitrack recorder and microphones available for one neighborhood recording session.
shared_context.S2: The session would use the small stage in the community room on a mutually agreed evening.
shared_context.S3: Marcus has asked about recording live music, and informal payment or barter terms are being discussed.
shared_context.S4: As part of the room's normal booking routine, Elena asks Marcus, Rina, and Dev for their concrete proposals or relevant booking details before she makes the final call and records the agreed terms.

PF1.text: Marcus's proposal is for Marcus to record three songs on Saturday from 18:00 to 20:00, with no cash payment and two private guitar lessons for Elena as the exchange.

PF2.text: Rina has offered Elena exactly $180 for the same recording setup on Sunday afternoon, but only if Rina may sell or otherwise commercially distribute the recording.

PF3.text: Dev learned from the community room manager this week that the room's recording license permits noncommercial use only and requires the final agreement to include a noncommercial-use commitment.

decisions.cash_alternative_recorded: integer — if PF2 is cited, record Rina's alternative as exactly 180 even if it was not selected

acceptance_conditions: The session must be accepted with Marcus as the recording partner.
The session must be scheduled for Saturday from 18:00 to 20:00.
The recording must cover exactly three songs.
The compensation must be exactly two private guitar lessons for Elena, with no cash payment.
The settlement must record Rina's exactly $180 cash alternative even though its commercial-use condition cannot be honored in the room.
The recording must be restricted to noncommercial use.
A noncommercial-use commitment must be logged for Marcus.
Elena must cite Dev's room-license fact when imposing the noncommercial-use restriction.

content_checks.C4: decisions['compensation_type'] in ['private guitar lessons', 'barter_guitar_lessons', 'guitar_lessons', 'private_guitar_lessons', 'barter'] and decisions['compensation_quantity'] == 2 and (decisions.get('cash_payment') in ['none', 'no_cash', '0', 'zero'] or 'cash_payment' not in decisions)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['noncommercial_use', 'noncommercial-use commitment', 'noncommercial_use_commitment', 'noncommercial-use', 'use_restriction'] and c['target'] == 'Marcus' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Marcus's exact proposal changes the accepted partner to Marcus, fixes Saturday 18:00-20:00, fixes the recording at three songs, and fixes compensation at two private guitar lessons with no cash.
Rina's proposal changes the comparison record from no known cash benchmark to an exactly $180 alternative, even though its commercial-use condition makes it unavailable under the room license.

The room-license finding changes recording use from unspecified to noncommercial, rules out Rina's commercially conditioned offer, and requires a noncommercial-use commitment for Marcus with Dev's fact cited as the reason.
